data.title: Run a night on Catch before you run one for real.
data.lead: Tell us about your event and we’ll send you a private demo built around it: your application questions, sample guests, and the door on the night. Nothing is published, messaged or charged.
data.note: Priority-2 page (/demo/). Decision: request a private demo. Uses the built private sales demo: a reviewed blueprint, an invitation bound to the person’s verified phone or email, synthetic application review, reply preparation, guest admission and an assistance request, at most three sessions, and a form draft prepared from the reviewed setup afterwards. No self-serve sandbox.

data.title: Four things, in about ten minutes.

items.d: Sample applicants answer your own questions. Approve, waitlist or decline them.
See the message each person would get, and change it.
Run the door for a sample night: who’s here, who’s late, who’s new.
A guest asks for help on the night. See how it reaches you.

data.title: Not a generic tour. Your questions, your format.
data.lead: Send us your current form or tell us what you ask guests. We set up the demo with your questions, and after you’ve tried it, we can turn it into a draft form in your own account, ready to publish.
ticks: Your questions, set up for you
Sample guests only; no real names, numbers or payments
Afterwards, a draft of your form in Catch Host

rows.t: It’s private to you and opens with your phone number or email. You can open it up to three times before it expires on [N days].
Nothing you do in the demo is published, sent to anyone or charged.

data.title: About the demo.
items: Yes. It’s a practice run with sample guests. Nothing is charged, published or sent.
Why can’t I open a demo straight away?
Each demo is set up around your own event and questions, so we prepare it for you. It usually takes [one working day].
Only you. It opens with the phone number or email you gave us.
Can I use what I set up?
Yes. Afterwards we can turn your demo into a draft form in your own Catch account, ready for you to publish.
Of course. Start the free trial and make your first event; the demo is there if you’d like to practise first.
How long does the link last?
You can open it up to three times before it expires.
